basics.name: Glen Wright
basics.label: Researcher, Knowledge & Data Team – REN21
basics.summary: Researcher and policy analyst with expertise in marine governance, ocean energy, and renewable energy policy. Currently contributing to the Global Status Report at REN21, with a focus on ocean energy and systemic data-driven insights. Experienced in international negotiations, project management, data storytelling, and strategic communication.

work.name: REN21 – Renewable Energy Policy Network for the 21st Century
work.summary: Author and analyst contributing to the Global Status Report (GSR), focusing on ocean energy and COVID-19 impacts. Supports REN21’s knowledge products through strategic data curation, expert engagement, and editorial input.
highlights: Lead author of the Ocean Energy chapter for the GSR.
Analyzed impacts of the global health crisis on renewable energy trends.
Streamlined project and knowledge management processes using advanced computing tools.

work.name: IDDRI – Institute for Sustainable Development and International Relations
work.summary: Led research and global policy engagement on high seas biodiversity, regional governance, and ocean sustainability. Represented IDDRI in UN negotiations and high-level forums.
highlights: Co-developed the STRONG High Seas project and Marine Regions Forum.
Published 15+ peer-reviewed and policy publications including 'The Long and Winding Road'.
Spoke at UN conferences, wrote for Nature, and advised on marine treaty negotiations.

work.name: UNESCO – Marine World Heritage Programme
work.summary: Provided strategic input on potential World Heritage sites in international waters.
highlights: Drafted reports for UNESCO Member States.
Advised on engagement in UN-level marine policy negotiations.

volunteer.summary: Advocacy and campaign support for human rights initiatives.
Supported policy and outreach work on environmental issues.

education.summary: PhD thesis: ‘Marine Governance in an Industrialised Ocean’ focused on ocean energy policy in the UK. Published book with Earthscan (2017).
Award-winning postgraduate study in renewable energy and environmental law.
Upper Second Class Honours; first-class dissertation; WorldMUN Delegate.

awards.title: Dean’s Award (4 classes)
awards.summary: For academic excellence in Renewable Energy and Climate Law courses.

awards.title: EDO & Maddocks Student Writing Competition
awards.summary: Winner of a national environmental law writing competition.

certificates.name: TEFL (Teaching English as a Foreign Language)

publications.summary: Widely cited guide to the UN high seas treaty negotiations.

publications.name: Protect the Neglected Half of Our Blue Planet
publications.summary: Commentary advocating for better protection of the high seas.
